title: Examination, Diagnosis & Treatment Planning II — Test

mcqs.q: A primary goal of caries diagnosis in operative dentistry is:
opts: Immediate extraction of all carious teeth
mcqs.explain: Goals are early detection of incipient caries, limiting caries activity before major destruction (remineralisation/prevention), and identifying high-risk patients.

mcqs.q: Caries diagnostic methods are broadly classified into conventional, advanced, and:
mcqs.explain: The three classes are conventional, advanced methods, and additional diagnostic aids (e.g. pulp-vitality tests).

mcqs.q: Which set lists the CONVENTIONAL methods of caries diagnosis?
mcqs.explain: Conventional methods are visual inspection, tactile exploration and radiographs; the others are advanced or supplementary.

mcqs.q: On visual inspection, the earliest sign of an incipient smooth-surface lesion is:
opts: A distinct cavity with exposed dentine
mcqs.explain: Early incipient caries shows white chalkiness/loss of translucency; later there is discoloration, softening, shadowing and cavitation.

mcqs.q: In the ICDAS two-digit coding system, the first digit (0–9) represents the:
mcqs.explain: ICDAS uses two digits for treatment planning: first (0–9) = restorative status; second (0–6) = caries-lesion severity.

mcqs.q: An ICDAS severity code of 0 means:
opts: Sound surface — no caries after 5 s of air drying
First visual change seen only after drying
mcqs.explain: Code 0 = sound (no caries after 5 s drying); code 1 = first change after drying; codes rise to 6 = extensive cavity with visible dentine.

mcqs.q: An ICDAS code 4 lesion is characterised by:
opts: An underlying dark shadow from dentine
First visual change after drying only
A cavity involving more than half the surface
mcqs.explain: Code 4 = underlying dark dentinal shadow (usually without cavitation); codes 5 and 6 are distinct and extensive cavities with visible dentine.

mcqs.q: Regarding tactile exploration of pits and fissures, which statement is TRUE?
opts: It is not confirmatory and injudicious use may fracture enamel and transfer bacteria
A sharp explorer catch always confirms caries
It is the single most reliable test for occlusal caries
It should be done with maximum force
mcqs.explain: Tactile exploration is not confirmatory; a 'false catch' may reflect explorer sharpness, pit shape or force, and forceful use can fracture enamel, cavitate and spread bacteria.

mcqs.q: The two radiographic views most used to diagnose caries in operative dentistry are:
mcqs.explain: Bitewing and IOPA films diagnose primary and recurrent caries and assess proximity to the pulp horn.

mcqs.q: First-line treatment options for a non-cavitated white-spot lesion include all EXCEPT:
mcqs.explain: White-spot lesions are managed non-invasively with topical fluoride, CPP-ACP and resin infiltration (ICON); a crown is not indicated.

mcqs.q: CPP-ACP used for white-spot lesions stands for:
mcqs.explain: CPP-ACP (casein phosphopeptide–amorphous calcium phosphate, e.g. GC Tooth Mousse) promotes remineralisation of early lesions.

mcqs.q: In diagnosing NON-cavitated proximal caries, use of an explorer:
opts: Must be done with caution, as excess force can penetrate intact surface over demineralised enamel
Should be forceful to confirm the lesion
mcqs.explain: Excessive exploring force can break the intact surface over demineralised enamel; aids include unwaxed floss, bitewings and FOTI.

mcqs.q: When unwaxed dental floss is drawn through a proximal contact and it shreds or breaks, this suggests:
mcqs.explain: Shredding/breaking of unwaxed floss at a proximal area indicates rough margins from decalcified enamel — a sign of proximal caries.

mcqs.q: A distinguishing feature of root-surface caries is:
opts: Association with gingival recession and a softened, darker cavitated lesion
mcqs.explain: Root caries occurs where recession exposes root; it shows darker discoloration, possible symptoms, and active lesions are soft and cavitated.

mcqs.q: The working principle of fibre-optic transillumination (FOTI) is that:
opts: Light scatters more at carious tissue, so caries appears as a dark shadow
mcqs.explain: FOTI relies on light scattering: caries has a lower index of light transmission, appearing as a dark shadow against a light background.

mcqs.q: A claimed advantage of DIFOTI over conventional radiographs is that it can:
opts: Detect early/incipient and recurrent caries and cracks even before they show on radiographs
mcqs.explain: DIFOTI captures transillumination images with a CCD camera and can reveal early decay, recurrent caries and cracks before radiographic visibility.

mcqs.q: DEXIS CariVu detects occlusal, interproximal and recurrent lesions and cracks using:
mcqs.explain: CariVu uses near-infrared transillumination technology; lesions appear as dark areas, similar in appearance to radiographs.

mcqs.q: Caries-detection dyes assist the clinician by:
opts: Differentially staining infected dentine to distinguish it from affected dentine
mcqs.explain: Dyes stain infected dentine (to be removed) more than affected dentine (to be preserved) — the principle of differential staining.

mcqs.q: In QLF, cariogenic-bacteria porphyrins and healthy enamel fluoresce, respectively:
mcqs.explain: Under QLF's high-energy/blue light, porphyrins of cariogenic bacteria fluoresce red while healthy enamel fluoresces green; reduced fluorescence indicates demineralisation.

mcqs.q: DIAGNOdent detects hidden and incipient caries by measuring:
opts: Laser-induced fluorescence, shown as a value 0–99
mcqs.explain: DIAGNOdent is a battery-operated diode-laser device; decay emits fluorescent light read by a sensor and displayed as a numeric value 0–99.

mcqs.q: The principle behind electrical-conductance caries detection (e.g. CarieScan PRO) is that demineralised enamel:
opts: Has increased electrical conductivity because of microscopic porosities
mcqs.explain: Healthy enamel is a poor conductor; demineralisation creates porous spaces that increase conductivity — higher readings indicate caries is likely.

mcqs.q: An advantage of digital radiography over conventional film is:
opts: No darkroom chemicals/odour and images can be transferred and enhanced
Higher radiation dose to the patient
Fixed contrast that cannot be adjusted
mcqs.explain: Digital imaging removes darkroom hazards, allows transfer/multi-site viewing, needs less storage, tags images with data, and permits contrast/resolution adjustment.

mcqs.q: A refrigerant spray such as Endo-Ice applied to a tooth is used to assess:
mcqs.explain: Endo-Ice is a cold thermal test of pulp vitality; the electric pulp tester is another additional diagnostic aid.

mcqs.q: A treatment plan is best defined as:
opts: A sequenced series of services to eliminate etiology, repair damage and maintain health
A list of the patient's presenting complaints
The fee estimate for the proposed treatment
mcqs.explain: A treatment plan is a carefully sequenced series of services designed to control etiologic factors, repair existing damage and create a functional, maintainable environment.

mcqs.q: Which is managed in the PRELIMINARY / EMERGENCY phase of treatment planning?
opts: Incision and drainage of an abscess
Placement of a fixed partial denture
mcqs.explain: The emergency phase controls pain/acute infection: extraction of painful teeth, incision & drainage, management of trauma and pulpectomy.

mcqs.q: Scaling, root planing, oral-hygiene instruction, caries control and replacing defective restorations belong to:
mcqs.explain: Phase 1 (control) stabilises dental health and removes etiologic factors — eliminating active disease and beginning prevention.

mcqs.q: Endodontic therapy and periodontal surgery (including implants) are carried out in:
mcqs.explain: Phase II includes periodontal surgery/implant placement and endodontic therapy; Phase III restores esthetics/function (prostho, ortho).

mcqs.q: Restoration of esthetics and function with fixed/removable prosthodontics and orthodontics is:
mcqs.explain: Phase III delivers definitive restoration of esthetics and function — prosthodontic and orthodontic treatment.

mcqs.q: A patient at HIGH risk of caries and periodontal breakdown should be recalled every:
mcqs.explain: Recall intervals: high risk every 3 months, moderate/medium every 4–6 months, and low risk every 9–12 months.

mcqs.q: A patient at LOW caries risk with good periodontal health is examined at intervals of:
mcqs.explain: Low-risk patients are recalled at 9–12 months; moderate risk 4–6 months; high risk 3 months.

saqs.q: State the goals of caries diagnosis and list the methods used for early detection.
saqs.a: GOALS — early detection of incipient caries; limiting activity before significant destruction, by remineralisation and prevention; identifying high-risk patients. METHODS — subsurface demineralization (vision, radiographs, dye); bacterial testing (S. mutans); salivary analysis (pH, flow, buffering); advanced methods (DIAGNOdent, QLF, FOTI, electrical conductance).

list: Limitation of caries activity before significant destruction — remineralisation and preventive methods

saqs.q: Describe the ICDAS system, including its two-digit code and the severity scale.
saqs.a: ICDAS is a visual clinical scoring system for education, practice, research and epidemiology. Two-digit code: first digit 0–9 restorative status, second 0–6 lesion severity. 0 sound · 1 change only after drying · 2 distinct change when wet · 3 localised enamel breakdown, no dentine · 4 dark dentinal shadow · 5 distinct cavity with dentine · 6 extensive cavity >½ surface.

ans.text: ICDAS — International Caries Detection and Assessment System, a visual clinical scoring system for education, practice, research and epidemiology. For treatment planning a two-digit code is used: the first digit (0–9) records the restorative status of the tooth, the second (0–6) the caries-lesion severity.

saqs.q: Compare the conventional methods of caries diagnosis and note the caution for tactile exploration.
saqs.a: VISUAL — white chalkiness, colour change, softening, shadowing, cavitation, loss of translucency. TACTILE — softening at the base of a pit/fissure and opacity around it, but a 'false catch' can mislead; NOT confirmatory, and injudicious use may fracture enamel, create a cavity and transfer bacteria. RADIOGRAPHS — bitewing and IOPA, for primary and recurrent caries and pulp proximity.

softening at the base of a pit or fissure and opacity of surrounding enamel — but a 'false catch' can result from a sharp explorer, the pit shape, or the force applied
bitewing and IOPA — primary and recurrent caries, and proximity to the pulp horn

saqs.q: Outline the advanced caries-detection methods by category with an example of each.
saqs.a: VISUAL ADVANCES — FOTI, DIFOTI (CariVu, DIAGNOcam), caries-detection dyes. FLUORESCENCE — DIAGNOdent (0–99), QLF, CamX Spectra. RADIOGRAPHIC — digital imaging. ELECTRICAL CONDUCTANCE — electronic caries monitor, CarieScan PRO.

head: Category
Examples
rows: FOTI — light scatters at caries producing a dark shadow. DIFOTI — CCD-captured images, detecting early/recurrent caries and cracks before radiographs (DEXIS CariVu, KaVo DIAGNOcam, near-infrared). Caries-detection dyes — differential staining of infected vs affected dentine

DIAGNOdent — laser fluorescence, value 0–99. QLF — blue light; caries porphyrins fluoresce red, enamel green; measures mineral loss over time. CamX Spectra — light-induced fluorescence with a colour scale
electronic caries monitor · CarieScan PRO — demineralisation increases conductivity

saqs.q: Explain how proximal caries is diagnosed (non-cavitated vs cavitated) and the aids used.
saqs.a: NON-CAVITATED — surface intact (explore with caution), radiolucency may be present, marginal ridge not discoloured, opaque area on FOTI. CAVITATED — surface broken, marginal ridge may be discoloured, opaque area in dentine on transillumination, radiolucency present. AIDS — visual and tactile, unwaxed floss (shreds on rough margins), bitewings, FOTI.

CAVITATED
rows: surface intact — an explorer must be used with caution, since excess force can penetrate intact surface over demineralised enamel
surface broken — detectable visually or tactilely; temporary mechanical separation may help

list: Unwaxed dental floss — breaks or shreds over rough decalcified margins

saqs.q: Describe the sequence of treatment planning phases and the recall intervals in the maintenance phase.
saqs.a: PRELIMINARY/EMERGENCY — treat emergencies first. PHASE 1 (control) — eliminate active disease and etiology. PHASE II — periodontal surgery, implants, endodontics. PHASE III — esthetics and function: fixed, removable, orthodontics. MAINTENANCE recall — low risk 9–12 months, moderate 4–6 months, high risk 3 months.

head: Phase
Content
rows: review the condition and history, treat emergencies first — control pain and acute infection, extract painful teeth, incise and drain abscesses, manage trauma, pulpectomy for acute pain

eliminate active disease (caries, inflammation), correct conditions limiting oral hygiene, remove etiologic factors, begin prevention — scaling, root planing, OHI, caries control, replacing or repairing defective restorations
periodontal surgery including implant placement, and endodontic therapy
restoration of esthetics and function — fixed and removable prosthodontics, orthodontics
